deep.reconstruction:
This page is a practical metrological and monetary table, not mathematics. It answers two questions for each coin type: how many pieces make up one Hanoverian pound by weight, and what that pound of coins is worth in Reichsthaler (Rth) and gute Groschen (ggr).

Units used: 1 Rth = 24 ggr; 1 ggr = 12 Pfennig (pf). The Hanoverian pound equals 2 Cologne marks, about 467.7 g.

The header reads 'Auf 1 Pfund Hannoverisch'. The table has three columns:
- Left: the denomination.
- Right: the number of pieces per pound, N.
- Middle: the face value of one pound of such coins, V = N × denomination.

Rows (my verification of the arithmetic):
1. 2 Rth Vereinsthaler: N = 12 3/5 (not 12 1/6). V = 25.2 Rth = 25 Rth 4 ggr 9.6 pf. Gauss writes '25 Rth 4 ...'.
   - Check from the 1838 Dresden coinage standard: 7 double thalers per fine mark at 0.900 fine give 6.3 per raw mark, hence 12.6 per pound.
   - The stray marginal '176.4' equals 12.6 × 14, i.e. 25.2 × 7; its purpose is uncertain.
2. 1 Rth: N = 21, V = 21 Rth.
   - Check: 14-thaler standard at 0.750 fine gives 10.5 per raw mark, hence 21 per pound; the piece weighs about 22.27 g.
3. 4 ggr (1/6 Thaler): N = 87 1/2. V = 350 ggr = 14 Rth 14 ggr (since 350 = 14·24 + 14). The piece weighs about 5.345 g.
4. 2 ggr: N = 175. V = 350 ggr = 14 Rth 14 ggr.
5. 1 ggr: N = 240. V = 240 ggr = 10 Rth.
6. 6 pf: N = 336. V = 2016 pf = 168 ggr = 7 Rth.
7. 4 pf: N = 504. V = 2016 pf = 7 Rth.
8. Hannoversche Pistole: N = 70 1/3, giving about 6.65 g per piece. The value entry ('8 1/4', '304') is unclear; at 5 Rth per pistole the face value would be 351 2/3 Rth.

The point of the table: full-weight silver (thalers) carries about 21 Rth of face value per pound. The 1/6–1/12 pieces carry only 14 7/12 Rth, groschen 10 Rth and pfennig coins 7 Rth, because the small change is debased.

Inverted section (page turned over): a list of individual coin weights. The units appear to be Dutch/Cologne 'As', with 1 As ≈ 0.0481 g (4864 As = 1 Cologne mark); this is my inference. Entries:
- Neue (Preuß.) Thaler 463.0 As ≈ 22.26 g
- pr. Louisd'or 138.5 As ≈ 6.66 g
- N.R. 1/6-type piece 110.9 As ≈ 5.33 g
- Hess. 1/6 109.4 As ≈ 5.26 g
- Hann. 1/12 43.0 As ≈ 2.07 g
- Hann. Mariengroschen 20.2 As ≈ 0.97 g

Further inverted items:
- Lines '— breite 1310 = (63,44)' and '— in g. 1337 = (64,72)' give paired measurements of some kind.
- Lines '1 = 52968' and '22 = 116753' are of unclear purpose.
- A note '63.538' also appears.
- There is an address note: 'Benjamin Rohnsfeld in Bremke'.
- There is a dated note: '♀ 13 Jun 18.. 11h Nachm.'.
errors: No arithmetic errors detected in the reconstructable rows. Every value entry equals N × denomination (25.2, 21, 14 Rth 14 ggr twice, 10, 7, 7 Rth).
The machine reading '12 1/6' for the 2-Rth row is inconsistent with the value 25 Rth 4+ ggr and with the coinage standard. 12 3/5 fits both.

The date reading '13 Jun 1811' cannot be right with the Venus (Friday) sign, since 13 June 1811 was a Thursday. Friday 13 June fell in 1817, 1828, 1834, 1845 and 1851. Because the 2-thaler Vereinsthaler dates from 1838 onward, the table itself is post-1838; the date note may be separate.

results.what: Table of the number of coins per Hanoverian pound and the face value per pound, for coins from 2 Rth down to 4 pf and the Pistole.
results.usually_credited_to: Routine 19th-century monetary metrology (Dresden Coinage Convention 1838, Prussian 14-thaler standard)

results.what: List of individual coin weights (in As) for Prussian, Hessian and Hanoverian coins.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a household and metrological memorandum of coin counts and values per pound. The arithmetic is trivial and contains no mathematical content of research interest.

checkable.asserts: 12 3/5 double thalers have a face value of 25.2 Rth.
0.2 Rth = 4.8 ggr, so 25.2 Rth = 25 Rth 4 4/5 ggr.
7 double thalers per fine mark at 0.9 fine, over 2 marks per pound, gives 12.6 pieces per pound.
The 14-thaler standard at 0.75 fine gives 21 thalers per Hanoverian pound.
463 As ≈ 22.26 g, the weight of the 14-thaler-standard thaler.

transcription_corrections: '12 1/6' in the 2 Rth row should read '12 3/5'.
'142 ʃ 14 ggr' in the 4 ggr row should read '14 Rth 14 ggr' (overwritten digits).
'ʃ' in the value column is Gauss's sign for Reichsthaler.
'504 [?]' in the 4 pf row is confirmed as 504 (it looks like '50H' in the image).
'7 ʃ — ₰ über 4 ʃ' is roughly '7 Rth — ' plus an unclear marginal note.
The year in '♀ 13 Jun 1811' is doubtful, since that date was not a Friday.
